Out-of-Core Block Sources

Source: R/block_source.R
block_source.Rd

A block source describes a list of data blocks without holding them in memory. Fitting functions that accept a block source (currently [aligned_mfa()]) read it one column chunk of one block at a time, so peak memory is one chunk plus the method's small summary statistics.

Usage

block_source(
  loader,
  nrow,
  ncol,
  names = NULL,
  colnames = NULL,
  chunk_size = 5000L
)

as_block_source(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'muscal_block_source'
as_block_source(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'list'
as_block_source(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_block_source(x, ...)

read_block(x, k, cols = NULL)

Arguments

loader

Function `function(k, cols)` returning block `k` restricted to the integer column indices `cols`, as a numeric matrix with `nrow[k]` rows and `length(cols)` columns. Every call for block `k` must return the rows in the same order. Missing and infinite values are not supported.

nrow, ncol

Integer vectors giving the number of rows and columns of each block.

names

Optional block names; defaults to `names(nrow)` or `X1, X2, ...`.

colnames

Optional list of column-name vectors, one per block (each `NULL` or of length `ncol[k]`). Needed for `feature_groups = "colnames"` or for feature groups that refer to features by name.

chunk_size

Maximum number of columns read per call to `loader`. Peak memory per read is about `8 * nrow[k] * chunk_size` bytes.

x

An object to convert: a list of matrices/data frames, or an existing block source.

...

Passed to `block_source()` (e.g. `chunk_size`).

k

Block index or name.

cols

Integer column indices to read; defaults to all columns.

Value

An object of class `muscal_block_source`.

For `read_block()`, the requested numeric matrix.

Details

`block_source()` wraps a loader function, which is the general mechanism: any storage (HDF5, file-backed matrices, NIfTI volumes, a database) can be exposed by writing `loader(k, cols)`. `as_block_source()` converts an in-memory list of matrices, which is mainly useful for testing the out-of-core code paths against the in-memory ones.

Examples

X <- list(A = matrix(rnorm(40), 10), B = matrix(rnorm(60), 10))
src <- block_source(
  loader = function(k, cols) X[[k]][, cols, drop = FALSE],
  nrow = c(10, 10), ncol = c(4, 6), names = c("A", "B"), chunk_size = 3
)
src
#> <muscal_block_source> 2 blocks, chunk_size = 3
#>  block nrow ncol
#>      A   10    4
#>      B   10    6
